question: I have a free day in San Francisco before the hackathon. Plan it for me.

guardian.answer:
Good morning! Since you're in San Francisco for the hackathon at 33 New Montgomery and don't have a car, let's plan a fantastic day focused on walking and making the most of that golden hour. Remember, no museums and nothing past 9 PM.

Here's a possible itinerary:

*   **Morning (10:00 AM - 12:00 PM): North Beach Exploration & Coffee**
    Start your day with a walk to North Beach, San Francisco's Little Italy. It's a vibrant neighborhood with a rich history. Grab a coffee and a pastry at a local cafe and soak in the atmosphere. You can wander through City Lights Bookstore, a famous literary landmark, or explore Washington Square Park.

*   **Lunch (12:00 PM - 1:00 PM): Budget-Friendly Bites in North Beach**
    North Beach has plenty of affordable and delicious Italian deli sandwiches or pizza by the slice options perfect for a budget-conscious meal.

*   **Afternoon (1:00 PM - 4:00 PM): Walk to Coit Tower & Panoramic Views**
    From North Beach, it's a pleasant walk up to Coit Tower. You can take the stairs if you're feeling energetic, or the paved path. The views from the top are absolutely stunning, offering panoramic vistas of the city, Alcatraz, and the Golden Gate Bridge – perfect for pre-golden hour scouting.

*   **Late Afternoon / Golden Hour (4:00 PM - 7:00 PM): Stroll along the Embarcadero & Ferry Building**
    Walk down from Coit Tower towards the Embarcadero. This waterfront promenade is beautiful, especially as the sun starts to dip. The Ferry Building Marketplace is a fantastic spot to explore, even if you're just window shopping or grabbing a small snack from one of its many artisan vendors. You'll get some incredible golden hour views of the Bay Bridge from here.

*   **Dinner (7:00 PM - 8:30 PM): Casual Dinner near the Embarcadero**
    There are several casual and budget-friendly eateries around the Ferry Building or a short walk away. You could grab some delicious tacos or a hearty bowl of clam chowder.

*   **Evening (8:30 PM - 9:00 PM): Easy Walk Back**
    As it approaches 9 PM, you can enjoy a leisurely walk back to your accommodation, enjoying the city lights.

This plan keeps you active, offers great views, and respects your evening preference for early nights. Let me know if you'd like any adjustments!

allMemories.title: Walk the entire city - no transit, 20k steps a day
allMemories.body: Decided that walking is how I experience San Francisco and I am building every itinerary around it. Rationale: the city is only seven miles across so nothing is truly far; the best moments on my last four trips were streets I stumbled onto between planned stop

allMemories.title: Museum-first itineraries - anchor every day on a major museum
allMemories.body: Locking in museums as the backbone of my travel planning. Every day should anchor on at least one serious institution and everything else fills in around it. Rationale: museums are climate-controlled anchors that work regardless of weather; they give me the hi

allMemories.title: Skip ticketed attractions - they eat the whole day
allMemories.body:
Done pre-booking marquee sites. A timed ticket turns a flexible day into a commute toward one appointment, and Alcatraz in particular burns four hours for a boat ride. Free and open-access places only from here. The advance-booking decision is superseded.

allMemories.title: Live music is the point - build nights around late shows
allMemories.body: Decided that live music venues are the reason I pick cities and San Francisco is the clearest case. Rationale: The Fillmore is a room with actual history and seeing anything there beats seeing the same act anywhere else; the Castro Theatre programming - sing-a

allMemories.title: Stop routing me through museums
allMemories.body:
Museums are not landing for me anymore - I have been indoors under fluorescent light for a year of work and I do not want to spend a free day the same way. Stop making them the anchor. Outdoors and open air by default now.

allMemories.title: The Pier 45 recommendation was a miss
allMemories.body:
Pier 45 and the Musee Mecanique got recommended as a highlight and it was a tourist crush with nothing to actually look at. Do not route me through the waterfront tourist strip again unless there is a specific reason.

allMemories.title: Early nights now - nothing scheduled past 9pm
allMemories.body:
Sleep has become the thing that determines whether the next day works. No shows, no late seatings, nothing that starts after 9pm. Sunset is the target for the last activity of the day. The late-show decision is superseded.
Tags: evening, sleep, schedule, super

allMemories.title: Golden hour is the planning constraint
allMemories.body:
Emerging pattern: I want the last outdoor stop timed to sunset rather than squeezed in before dinner. Coastal and elevated viewpoints specifically. Plan backward from golden hour.
Tags: golden hour, sunset, outdoors, planning.
This was recorded 12 days ago.

allMemories.title: Self-guided over group tours, always
allMemories.body: Consistent preference across trips: I do not book guided group tours. I would rather read ahead and walk it myself at my own pace than be moved through a site on someone else's clock. Audio guides are fine. Private guides are fine if the site genuinely require

allMemories.title: Batteries to Bluffs was exactly right
allMemories.body:
The Batteries to Bluffs Trail suggestion was the best thing recommended to me all year - outdoors, coastal, no ticket, no crowd, and I set my own pace. More of this shape.
Tags: feedback, Batteries to Bluffs Trail, outdoors, trail, positive.

allMemories.title: No car this trip
allMemories.body:
Not renting a car on this trip. Anything that requires driving is out - it needs to be walkable from transit or it does not happen.
Tags: context, transit, no car, current trip.
This was recorded 3 days ago.

allMemories.title: Knee injury - walking radius capped, transit-adjacent only
allMemories.body:
Tore something in my right knee. Hard cap of three miles total on foot per day and no sustained hills. Everything now has to be transit-adjacent or it does not go on the itinerary. The walk-everywhere decision is superseded.
Tags: mobility, accessibility, knee

allMemories.title: Photo-first traveler - recognition is the primary interaction
allMemories.body: How I actually use a travel assistant: I photograph a building I am standing in front of and want to know what it is and whether it matters. The Shell Building and the Golden Coin Building are both cases where I had the photo before I had the name. Scene recog
